validated_results.title: Risk of Alcohol Consumption in Bladder Cancer: Case-Control Study from a Nationwide Inpatient Database in Japan.
validated_results.journal: The Tohoku journal of experimental medicine
validated_results.reason: Original matched case-control study reporting an adjusted odds ratio for alcohol consumption and incident bladder cancer.

extraction.population: Japanese inpatients in the nationwide Rosai Hospital group clinical database

sample_size.excerpt: We identified 739 cases of bladder cancer diagnosed between 2005 (when the database was established) and 2014 and 7,196 controls matched by sex, age, hospital, and admission period.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 739 + 7196 = 7935

cases.excerpt: We identified 739 cases of bladder cancer diagnosed between 2005 (when the database was established) and 2014 and 7,196 controls matched by sex, age, hospital, and admission period.

effect_size.excerpt: The risk of bladder cancer was significantly higher in ever drinkers than in never drinkers (odds ratio, 1.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.06 to 1.66).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The risk of bladder cancer was significantly higher in ever drinkers than in never drinkers (odds ratio, 1.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.06 to 1.66).

comparison.excerpt: higher in ever drinkers than in never drinkers

design.excerpt: The study was a matched case-control study from the nationwide Japanese clinical database

continent.excerpt: nationwide Japanese clinical database administered by the Rosai Hospital group

ethnicity.excerpt: Among Japanese, alcohol consumption may be an independent risk factor for bladder cancer

exposure_measurement.excerpt: We estimated the odds ratio of alcohol consumption for bladder cancer adjusted for the amount of smoking, high-risk occupations, and comorbidities

gender.excerpt: 7,196 controls matched by sex, age, hospital, and admission period

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_basis: Population imputation: stated Asian country/population -> Asian
extraction.ethnicity_supporting_text: Among Japanese, alcohol consumption may be an independent risk factor for bladder cancer

validated_results.title: Association between selected dietary scores and the risk of urothelial cell carcinoma: A prospective cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort reporting hazard ratios for the Mediterranean Diet Score and incident urothelial cell carcinoma of the bladder.

extraction.comparison_type: Per one standard deviation increase in Mediterranean Diet Score (invasive urothelial cell carcinoma)
extraction.timing: Baseline dietary assessment with median 21.3 years follow-up
extraction.population: Adults in a prospective cohort with baseline food frequency questionnaire

cases.excerpt: Over a median follow-up time of 21.3 years, 379 incident UCC cases were diagnosed.

effect_size.excerpt: A healthier diet was found to be inversely associated with the risk of invasive (MDS: HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.74-1.00, metascore: HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.71-0.98), but not superficial disease (heterogeneity between subtypes p = 0.04 and p = 0.03, respectively).

confidence_interval.excerpt: A healthier diet was found to be inversely associated with the risk of invasive (MDS: HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.74-1.00, metascore: HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.71-0.98), but not superficial disease (heterogeneity between subtypes p = 0.04 and p = 0.03, respectively).

comparison.excerpt: We used Cox models to compute hazard ratios (HR) for the association between dietary scores (per one standard deviation) and UCC risk.

design.excerpt: Association between selected dietary scores and the risk of urothelial cell carcinoma: A prospective cohort study.

timing.excerpt: Dietary scores were calculated using data from a 121-item food frequency questionnaire administered at baseline.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary scores were calculated using data from a 121-item food frequency questionnaire administered at baseline.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
